title: Fix reimporting saved-to-file meshes clearing surface override materials

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Fixes #79779

When a mesh from an imported scene is saved to a file with **Save to File** in the Advanced Import Settings, reimporting the source file while a scene that uses the mesh is open clears the surface override materials of every `MeshInstance3D` using it. Saving the scene afterwards writes the loss to disk.

## Root Cause

For meshes saved to file, `ResourceImporterScene::_generate_meshes()` refills the cached `ArrayMesh` in place.. it calls `reset_state()` on it and passes it to `ImporterMesh::get_mesh()` as the base mesh. `get_mesh()` emits `changed` at every step of the rebuild: once when the name is set, while the mesh still has no surfaces, and again for each surface added, material set and surface name set.

`MeshInstance3D::_mesh_changed()` resizes `surface_override_materials` to the mesh's current surface count on every emission, so the overrides of surfaces that haven't been re-added yet are dropped.

## Symptoms

- Surface override materials become `<null>` on every node using the mesh, and saving the scene removes its `surface_material_override/*` properties
- Blend shape values set on those nodes reset to 0
- The viewport keeps on rendering old materials, so the loss only shows up after the scene is saved and reopened
- `SoftBody3D` is affected the same way, since it inherits from `MeshInstance3D`

## Additional information

`get_mesh()` now wraps the rebuild in `_block_emit_changed()` / `_unblock_emit_changed()`, the same batching `Resource::copy_from()` uses since #102650, so the mesh emits `changed` once, after it's fully built.

- Both methods are protected members of `Resource`, so `ArrayMesh` declares `ImporterMesh` as a friend.
- Scripts connected to the mesh's `changed` signal now get a single emission instead of one per step.
- Not covered: import scripts that modify the cached mesh themselves, and meshes reloaded from `.tres`/`.tscn` files (#121023, which #123055 addresses).

I also have a unit test ready that rebuilds a base mesh in place the way the importer does, and checks that surface override materials and blend shape values are kept and that `changed` is emitted once. I left it out to keep the review surface small, since fixes in this area don't usually add new tests, but I'm happy to add it.

Tested on master and 4.7 with the steps from the issue and from #85850.

**AI disclosure:** I designed the test plan, wrote, and reviewed the changes. Opus was used for initial research and localized testing.
